title: Does mlumr's ML-UMR agree with an independent g-computation and carry exactly the analytic omitted-covariate bias?
question: With no second implementation of unanchored ML-UMR and no multinma overlap, does mlumr's transported absolute outcome agree with an independent g-computation, reduce correctly in the individual data's own population, and show exactly the bias theory predicts when a prognostic covariate is omitted?
design: Unanchored binary-outcome comparison, individual data on the index treatment and published summaries on the comparator; an unreported prognostic covariate of none, moderate or strong effect at two overlap levels; mlumr (installed commit 006b604) against an independent g-computation, mlumr::stc and mlumr::naive. 6 cells, 200 replicates each.
